Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: In these two rules question calls for determination are same whether the loanee judgment debtor could maintain his property on payment of decretal amount.

2. In Civil Revision No. 941 of 2005 it is the case of the petitioner that Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation sanctioned loan of Taka 7,90,000 at 5% simple interest on 23-3-1979 in favour of loanee, Md Khurshed Alam Khusnavish, for constructing a 3 storied home in Kha schedule land but the loanee defaulted in paying installment and its stands at Taka 15,23,342,86 and the defaulter loanee was bound to pay the entire amount at a time, hence, the Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 1999 was instituted.

3. In Civil Revision No. 1372 of 2004, the case is that Taka 5,91,000 was sanctioned as loan by Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation in favour of the judgment debtor for construction of 3-storied residential house in Kha schedule land with 7.5% interest but loanee defaulted in payment of the loan and when it stands at Taka 12,09,618.61, the case was filed.

4. Both the cases were decreed ex-parte by the learned District Judge, Tangail. Thereafter, Money Execution Case No. 6 of 2002 and Money execution Case No. 11 of 2001 were filed. The petitioner of both the rules appeared and filed objection but the said objection having been refused, the present rules from that Order of refusal.

5. Mr Abul Quasem, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners of both the rules, submits that, despite the decision of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation vs Phan Ara Akhter, 49 DLR (AD) 80 wherein it has been settled that the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation is not at all a financial institution within meaning of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 and also 2003 but Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation has been incorporated under section 2 Ka(4) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as such the same should be excluded from the definition clause of Ain, 2003. On the merit of the case, Mr Abdul Quasar, learned Advocate, submits that Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation acted as beneficial of the people of Bangladesh. Learned Advocate submits that section 27 deals with realization of loan sanctioned by Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation. Learned Advocate further submits that, no notice was served while the ex-parte decree was pronounced and it is not available from the record when the ex-parte decree was passed whether the case was ready for hearing or not, as such the judgments and orders impugned are liable to be set aside.

6. Mr Shaheed Alam, learned Advocate on the other hand submits that, the petitioner was aware of the entire proceedings related to institution of the suit up to the ex-parte decree. The learned Advocate further submits that from the record it appears that Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation instituted the suit at first before the Artha Rin Adalat but later on, as per aforesaid decision of the Appellate Division it was transferred to the Court of District Judge, as such, it can safely be said that the cases were instituted legally after complying all the required formalities. Let us proceed with our judgment.

<u>7. On the question of removal the name of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation from the definition clause of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, we find that the Appellate Division pronounce the judgment on 22-7-1996 i.e. long before coming into force of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. It is very unfortunate that Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs still did not act as per the decision of 49 DLR (AD) 80 and 47 DLR 158 thereby causes hindrance in the matter of administration of Justice. We hope that in no time Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs will act as per the aforesaid decisions and delete House Building Finance Corporation from section 2 Ka(4) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.</u>

<u>8. Let us take up civil revision 941 of 2005 at first. We have consulted the order sheet of Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1998. This case was first instituted before Artha Rin Adalat, Tangail on 25-6-95 and it continued upto 27-1-97 when the decision of 49 DLR was produced before the Court and the case record was sent to the learned District Judge, Tangail where it is registered on 24-5-98 as Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1998. It appears from order dated 30-9-98 that :—</u>

<u>“আদালত যোগে জারীর নোটিশ জারী হইয়াছে। রেজিঃ নোটিশ দাখিল না করায় উহা ইস্যু করা হয় নাই।”</u>

9. Thereafter, from order No. 4 up to order No. 20 dated 16-8-2001 summons were not served. From Order No. 21 dated 22-11-2001 it appears that the learned Judge recorded as: “অত্র মামলার প্রতিপক্ষের নামীয় জেজিঃ নোটিশ জারী অন্তে এ/ডি ফেরত আসিয়াছে।” Then the learned Judge fixed on 14-1-2002 for ex-parte disposal. Ex-parte decree was passed on 27-4-2002. The heirs of original loanee filed objection and Miscellaneous Case No. 29 of 2002 was started.

10. It appears from the order No. 29 dated 8-7-2002 that the learned Judge rejected the objection filed by the heirs of the Original loanee. Learned Judge held as:-

“ডিক্রী জারী দরখাস্ত হইতেই দেখা যায় যে, মূল দায়িক এর মৃত্যুতে তাহার ওয়ারিশদেরকে পক্ষ করা হইয়াছে। নিলামের ইস্তেহারের পূর্বেই ডিক্রীজারী মোকদ্দমায় দায়িক পক্ষকে নোটিশ দেওয়া হইয়াছে। অতঃপর নিলামের জন্য ধার্য্য করা হইয়াছে। কাজেই আইন সংগত ভাবেই সকল কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ করা হইয়াছে। তাহাছাড়া মূল মোকদ্দমায় বিচার বিশ্লেষণ করিয়াই ডিক্রী এর টাকার পরিমাণ ধার্য্য হইয়াছে।”

<u>11. On a consultation of the entire order sheet we do not find, save and except return of acknowledgment due, whether the original loanee or heirs have any knowledge of the proceeding. Substituting of heirs does not mean that they have knowledge and also the heirs are in know of the proceedings. Moreover, it appears that the learned judge while dismissing the Miscellaneous case took into consideration of the process servers' report but, process server was not examined. Learned Advocate for the Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation submits that, on reference of annexure-F than the petitioners are in know of the proceedings but it appears that this affidavit filed in support of the rule showing that judgment debtor No. 2 filed objection who he is in know of the fact of the case but from reading of this affidavit we do not find the judgment debtors were in known of the entire proceedings i.e. from filing of the case up to the ex-parte decree. Moreover, the averments made on 31-8-2004 i.e. long after the ex-parte decree passed in the instant case as ex-parte decree was passed on 2-4-2000 as such, by this affidavit it cannot be said that heirs of original loanee had knowledge of the proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1998.</u>

<u>12. Now, in respect of Civil Revision No. 1372 of 2004. It arises out of Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1995. It was decreed ex-parte on 27-4-2002 for an amount of Taka 15,47,901.74. House Building Finance Corporation filed Money Execution Case No. 6 of 2002 for realizing decreetal amount. Petitioner as soon as came to know of the execution case filed application for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that the petitioner deposited Taka 2,12,340 after the decree which was received by the decree holder. The learned Judge rejected said application. We have considered the entire order sheet of Miscellaneous Case 47 of 1998 as it was transferred to learned District Judge after the Judgment of 49 DLR (AD) 80. It appears from order No. 1 dated 24-5-98 up to order No. 20 dated 16-8-2001 that acknowledgment due was not returned. It returned, as it appears, from order No. 21 of 22-11-2001. The learned Judge fixed 14-1-2001 for ex-parte disposal of the case. The case ultimately decreed ex-parte on 27-4-2002.</u>

<u>13. In passing an ex-parte decree Court must be satisfied that summons /notices were duly served on the loanee and to have a satisfaction on service of summons Court must consider the process servers report and also the deposition of the process server or postal peon. It is the duty of the petitioner, Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, in whose favour the ex-parte decrees were passed, to prove service of summons by producing reliable evidence. Rule 19 of Order V of Code of Civil Procedure cast a duty upon Court to examine the postal peon/process server before passing an ex-parte decree. The Court ought to have consider the declaration of process server under Rule 19A of Order V of Code of Civil procedure as evidence before ex-parte decree is passed. Ex-parte decree speaks some fishy fishy in obtaining the same.</u>

<u>14. The Bangladesh House Building Corporation Finance Order, 1973 is a beneficial law to the people as it provide financial facilities for the construction, repair and remodeling of houses at any place in Bangladesh. The Corporation is to carry its affairs through a Board consisting of a Managing Director and not more than five other directors. Besides, the Corporation may appoint a standing committee of experts to be called the Technical Advisory Committee. Article 20 of PO 7 of 1973 empowers the Corporation to grant loan to borrowers. Article 21(1) speaks condition for granting loan as no loan can be sanctioned unless it is fully secured. Article 21(4) allow the Corporation to grant additional loan to a borrower. Article 21(8) speaks for mode of repayment of loan and it speaks for monthly installments. Article 25 empowers the Corporation to issue notice upon any borrower or surety for payment of the loan in full if there be any default in payment of loan and for some other breaches of terms of the conditions in obtaining the loan and further empower the Corporation under Article 26 of sell any property pledged, mortgaged etc. So far as I see PO 7 of 1973 is beneficial to any citizen for constructing homes as it lays its hand to help the citizen. Article 27 give forum for realisation of loan. On consideration of entire PO 7 of 1973 it is gathered that this law was promulgated for the welfare of a citizen providing financial assistance to make a home and is not so drastic that just on the failure of repayment, the schedule property given as security, automatically vest in the Corporation to be sold for realisation of loan money. As such I am of the view that on the event of failure for payment of loan the proceeding under Article 27 ought or should be completed giving full opportunity to the loanee to retain his/her property even there be decree passed either contested or ex-parte against loanee because the person know the misery of loosing the property.</u>

<u>15. In the decision of Abdul Jalil vs Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation reported in 41 DLR (AD) 108, it has been held that if the original loanee wanted to retain his property by satisfying the decree by paying decretal amount he may be allowed to do so.</u>

<u>16. Considering all these aspect of the case, we are of the view that, while decrees were passed there were no material before the Court to hold that the judgment debtors were in know of the proceedings of the case. We find substance in the rules.</u>

17. In the result, the rules are made absolute without any order as to costs.

<u>18. The ex-pate decree passed in both the rules are set aside. We are directing the learned Judge to proceed with the Miscellaneous Cases in accordance with law. If the judgment debtors wanted to retain their property by paying claim money of Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation, then they may be allowed to do so and in this case learned judge can disposed of the cases without taking any further step. Send down the lower record.</u>

Communicate this order at once.
